scope: Theorem 1 of the manuscript “Simulating One-Tape Time in Two-Fifths-Power Space” (preprints/Simulating-One-Tape-Time-in-Two-Fifths-Power-Space-September-25-2026/article.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 137 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 873c9e2790a66c53), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 2. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Fix a deterministic machine with one writable tape and head, a fixed number of read-only input heads, unit movement and fixed origins for all heads, cap-independent symbol functions, and a fixed accessor as above. For every public input x and supplied binary cap T ≥ 2 for which the access condition holds, its finite-control and halting outcome by time T can be computed deterministically in e O(T2/5) work-space bits, excluding storage for the read-only input. Simulation time is unrestricted, and the final writable tape need not be materialized. If the access condition holds for (x, T) at every T ≥ 2, and the machine halts on x after t steps without a supplied running time, its outcome can be computed in e O((t + 2)2/5) work-space bits.
